# Bars

*Describes reflex-silverpoint-react 0.8.1, wrapping silverpoint 0.8.0.*

Each chart's own props, with the JS name the silverpoint MCP tools and the React docs use. The props
every chart shares (`data`, `title`, `height`, `ground`, `palette`, the events…) are in
[SKILL.md](../../SKILL.md#common-chart-props); the defaults and notes of each prop come from the
MCP's `get_chart`. In each example the rows live in a `rx.State` field passed as `data`.

<!-- generated:family -->

**8 charts:** [`bar_chart`](#bar_chart) · [`stacked_bar_chart`](#stacked_bar_chart) · [`composed_chart`](#composed_chart) · [`waterfall_chart`](#waterfall_chart) · [`funnel_chart`](#funnel_chart) · [`bullet_chart`](#bullet_chart) · [`pyramid_chart`](#pyramid_chart) · [`candlestick_chart`](#candlestick_chart)

## bar_chart

`bar-chart` · `BarChart` · Pill bars, as columns or rows, with an optional second series.

Its own props (the common ones are in [SKILL.md](../../SKILL.md#common-chart-props)):

| Python | JS | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `x_key` | `xKey` | `Accessor<string \| number>` |
| `value_key` | `valueKey` | `Accessor<number \| null \| undefined>` |
| `secondary_key` | `secondaryKey` | `Accessor<number \| null \| undefined>` |
| `orientation` | `orientation` | `'columns' \| 'rows'` |

```python
import reflex as rx
from reflex_silverpoint_react import bar_chart


class State(rx.State):
    rows: list[dict] = []


def bar_chart_view() -> rx.Component:
    return bar_chart(
        data=State.rows, x_key="x", value_key="value", secondary_key="previous", title="Bar chart", id="bar-chart"
    )
```

The demo's first rows (read through x_key="x", value_key="value", secondary_key="previous"), drawn when `data` is omitted:

```json
[{"x": "Q1", "value": 42, "previous": 35}, {"x": "Q2", "value": 58, "previous": 44}, {"x": "Q3", "value": 51, "previous": 49}]
```

## stacked_bar_chart

`stacked-bar-chart` · `StackedBarChart` · One stacked segment per key.

Its own props (the common ones are in [SKILL.md](../../SKILL.md#common-chart-props)):

| Python | JS | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `x_key` | `xKey` | `Accessor<string \| number>` |
| `keys` | `keys` | `readonly string[]` |
| `names` | `names` | `readonly string[]` |

```python
import reflex as rx
from reflex_silverpoint_react import stacked_bar_chart


class State(rx.State):
    rows: list[dict] = []


def stacked_bar_chart_view() -> rx.Component:
    return stacked_bar_chart(
        data=State.rows,
        x_key="x",
        keys=["free", "pro", "team"],
        names=["Free", "Pro", "Team"],
        title="Stacked bar chart",
        id="stacked-bar-chart",
    )
```

The demo's first rows (read through x_key="x"), drawn when `data` is omitted:

```json
[{"x": "Jan", "free": 40, "pro": 18, "team": 6}, {"x": "Feb", "free": 46, "pro": 21, "team": 9}, {"x": "Mar", "free": 38, "pro": 26, "team": 11}]
```
